newsitem.title: USA: Big cut seen for U.S. food aid in fiscal year 1998.
newsitem.headline: Big cut seen for U.S. food aid in fiscal year 1998.

text.p: The major U.S. food aid program -- "Food for Peace" -- would be cut by more than $100 million in President Bill Clinton's proposed budget for fiscal 1998, a congressional source said on Thursday.

Clinton administration officials said there would be no cuts in two of the three parts of "Food for Peace" but did not offer direct assurance about Title I, which provides long-term concessional sales of U.S. agricultural exports to developing nations.

Congress appropriated $1.1 billion for "Food for Peace" for this fiscal year, enough to provide 3.2 million metric tons of food. The bulk of it, 2.2 million tons, would come through Title II donations for hunger and famine relief.

Title I would be cut by about $100 million for fiscal 1998, which begins on Oct. 1, the congressional source said, and a $50 million reduction would be sought from this year's funds. Some $240 million was appropriated for Title I this year, enough for 1.1 million metric tons of food assistance.

When asked about potential funding cuts, Brian Atwood, head of the Agency for International Development, said: "That's not the case, at least for Title II and III." AID runs those parts of "Food for Peace."
Title III of the program provides for government-to-government grants for use in economic development.
Gus Schumacher, the Agriculture Department official with jurisdiction over Title I, said he was obliged not to comment until the budget was proposed on Feb. 6.
"The president's budget is coming out shortly and we hope it provides good support," Schumacher said.
"Food for Peace" was created in 1954 to carry out the objectives of hunger relief, development of markets for U.S. farm exports, and encouraging economic development in developing countries.
It has been under budgetary pressure in recent years. For example, in fiscal 1995, it was alloted $1.29 billion, sufficient for 3.8 million metric tons of aid.
